title: Evaluation of the effects of a preventive training program to improve coordination and muscle strength depending on individual fitness
summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of a scientifically designed training program for improving coordination and muscle strength. Standardized physical examinations and questionnaire data are conducted at the beginning and end of the intervention (an eight-week, video-based training program). The results are then compared with those of the control group, which did not participate in the training program during the study period.
conditions: Preventive improvement of coordination and muscle strength as well as reduction of existing coordination problems

interventions.name:
The intervention group comprises a total of 150 participants, divided into three groups of 50 people each. Assignment to the individual groups is based on fitness level and the following age categories: 30–50 years, 50–70 years, and over 70 years.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Willingness to participate voluntarily
Exclusion criteria:
• Inability to stand or walk without support (e.g., need for a walker)
• Amputations
• Blindness
• Acute neurological conditions such as Parkinson's disease or dementia
• Severe polyneuropathies
• Significant muscular dystrophy
• Lack of technical equipment to complete the video-based exercise programs (e.g., laptop or tablet)
